newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil plans no pay rise for public workers - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil plans no pay rise for public workers - report.

text.p: Brazil's public sector workers will not receive a pay rise in 1997 because of a high court ruling in February granting a 28.86 percent wage hike to 11 civil servants, local O Globo newspaper said.
The government had been expected to raise civil servants' salaries by 10 percent this year, the first adjustment since 1995.

But the high court ruling, based on claims civil servants deserved the same pay rise as awarded to the armed services in 1993, led the government to decide it would not adjust salaries this year, according to Claudia Costin, executive-secretary of the Administration Ministry.

The decision by the Supreme Federal Tribunal is expected to encourage up to a million other past and present public workers to demand the same salary adjustment which would cost the federal government billions of dollars a year.

After a ministerial cabinet meeting to discuss the 1997 budget on Friday, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said that 1997 is "decisive" in the government's battle to balance its books and stabilize its growing debt stockpile.

Kandir reaffirmed the federal government was committed to achieving a primary budget surplus of 0.8 percent of gross domestic product and a primary surplus for the consolidated public sector of 1.5 percent of GDP.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
